submission.justification:
Radiator-R3 at 2 cm thickness is recommended as it achieves the best pion/kaon separation performance at 10 GeV/c among all candidates. Through systematic simulation:

PERFORMANCE ANALYSIS:
- R3 at 2 cm: 4.832σ separation (optimal)
- R1 at 3 cm: 3.8σ separation (optimal for R1)
- R2 at 3.5 cm: 2.933σ separation (optimal for R2)

R3 provides 27.2% better separation than R1 and 64.8% better than R2, representing a significant improvement in hadron identification capability.

LONGEVITY CONSIDERATION:
R3 is a porous silica aerogel. While porous materials can be susceptible to degradation, the project documents confirm that dry nitrogen protection will be implemented to prevent moisture absorption and maintain optical properties over the experiment's lifetime. R1 also has hydrophobic treatment as an additional safeguard, but R3's superior performance (4.832σ vs 3.8σ) outweighs this difference, especially with proper environmental protection in place.

CONSTRAINT COMPLIANCE:
- Thickness: 2 cm is within the required 1-6 cm range
- Candidate selection: R3 is one of the three listed candidates
- Performance maintenance: Achievable with dry nitrogen protection system
- Best separation: Clearly superior to all alternatives

The 2 cm thickness is optimal for R3, balancing photon statistics with chromatic effects to maximize separation power.
